From the three quotes that I received, only RenewCo bothered to come to my home and do a proper on site inspection. The other two wanted photos of my meter and the address. RenewCo were very professional and I would have gone with them if not for the price and the fact that they used optimisers (Solar edge) in their quote whereas I preferred micro inverters (Enphase). The panels from RenewCo were REC Alpha Pure R and the panels from Rescom were REC twinpeak 5. I know that the REC Alpha Pure R panels are better than the REC twinpeak 5, but they are not $4500 better. Also, seeing how Enphase micro inverters are dearer than SolarEdge optimisers, I found it hard to justify the cost difference. Furthermore, I received 15 years warranty on the micro inverters, compared to the 12 years warranty I was offered for the optimisers. Finally, the failure rate of micro inverters is lower than the failure rate of optimisers. I am very happy with my decision, and Rescom did a great job of the installation.

After getting more than 5 quotes, I spoke to Sam from Rescom who provided clear and helpful advice (without the up-sell - he suggested that waiting to see how the initial system performs before spending an extra $10K on a battery may be the best way to go). The quote of a little under $11K for a 12.35 kW system (Jinko panels, DC optimisers, SolarEdge inverters) was around the median - I obtained outlier quotes of less than $7K and more than $15K.The supply and installation occurred within 10 days of my acceptance of the quote. The installation itself was a smooth process taking about 4 hours.I couldn't turn my new system on for 3 weeks until the smart meter was installed, which was frustrating with a run of sunny skies but only partly the fault of Rescom for slightly delaying the submission of the request. My retailer, Dodo, needed to be chased up to have the smart meter installed.The system is now up and running, and generating >50 kWh per day on a sunny day. Thanks to Sam and Rescom for the support and service received to date.

I was very happy with the sales approach of this company after dealing with a number of very pushy sales people from other companies. The product offering was good value for money and the installation went very well, installers were communicative and punctual. So far so good with after sale support, I've only had a couple of questions and they have been answered promptly. I'm very happy with the system so far.

The fun stuff:Almost every one of the solar guys I bumped at checked my address online and would say 'your roof can only take a 4 to 6 Kw system, I promise!'. Then I'd send them my ugly panel-plan I made with PowerPoint and they'd come back instantly to do a 'panel-match-up'. This would happen every single time and I had fun while it lasted.Some were pretty good, some cowboys and for some I was just a potential to up their monthly target (one of the companies' rep actually said that she's running low on her target for the month and that I could help her by signing up!).I almost signed up with another company but backed off as their battery deal wasn't up my budget.The top solar-cowboy award goes to:The biggest of all the cowboy scheme was one of those leading energy providers whose solar division told me that they'd install their 'state-of-the-art' system with no upfront costs for me. They'd use all the energy from my panels, not me, paying me nothing, whilst I continue to pay through the nose to my energy provider for electricity & gas, and after 7 long years, the arguably 'state-of-the-art' system is mine! I wished them good luck to get customers.The research part:I took months to research on the solution, the panels, the inverter and the company I'd sign up with. Almost every solar provider would have my number with them or would have spoken to me at least once. I visited SolarQuotes.com.au almost everyday and got a lot of insights about the whole industry. Without this, I wouldn't have had the awareness of all those pitfalls and cowboys to avoid. So if you are exploring solar market, I'd strongly suggest to:- familiarize yourself with the terminologies- visit SolarQuotes.com.au and read as much as you can- prepare a spreadsheet with what you need and what's offered, this will save a lot of time for youThe facts part:Whilst I was about to sign up with another company, I read the reviews of RESCOM here in SolarQuotes and decided to contact them.Leon responded at once with a couple of options varying in capacity and insisted that he'd want to take a look at the roof in person. He was the only one of all the providers I reached out to said he'll visit my place to check the roof.There were discussions around what panels to choose, where to position them as my roof is not a plain north facing fairy tale roof. Once its finalized, the installation team notified me on a tentative date, it got moved due to the team members getting Covid, I was well informed in advance.The installation part:Absolute pro team. No noise, no power off, apart from the last few minutes when they connected the system. No debris left in my place. Clean walk through of what to do, and they left without a trace. The RESCOM team followed up with my energy provider to enable the system in theirs.Overall, without SolarQuotes website, I wouldn't have figured out a very good provider. Thank you guys!

Our system is made up of 25 x Jinko 415W N-Type panels, each paired with IQ7A Enphase Microinvertors. All black frames and rails were used, so it looks great with our dark roof. We purchased a house in Northern Sydney in April 2016 with a 14 panel Enphase system installed new and supposedly maintained by Rescom Solar Pty Ltd in August 2015. After a storm I inspected the system and found that the flimsy plastic conduit protecting the wiring was so degraded by the sun in 12 months it was cracked and leaking. The plastic isolator switches were not covered and had degraded in the sun and required replacing, the wiring between the panels was actually laying oin the roof tiles instead of being tied to the support frames and when I rang Alex at Rescom to get a service I did not get a reply to my several messages left on the answering machine. We employed another supplier to carry out the repairs at a cost of over $1200. I would not recommend Rescom Solar as a competent installer.
